claim: Merged concepts are not subsets of their parents: items are accepted in 'A and B' that are rejected from A alone (overextension), across words and pictures, and it is not explained by response noise or base rate.
agent_test: Ask the agent to judge membership of borderline items in A, B, A-and-B; check it shows human-like overextension; use as a probe of whether blends are treated as strict intersections.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Strong fit to one parent compensates for weak fit to the other, and one constituent usually dominates; combination is non-commutative (A which are B differs from B which are A).
agent_test: Run each seed pair in both orders at equal tokens and compare idea sets; test whether order-randomised pairs beat fixed-order.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Most attributes of a conjunction are inherited from the parents; truly emergent attributes are rare in intersective conjunctions (3 of 174 strict, 11 lenient) and arise from extensional feedback or scenario construction.
schema_part: O (combine) / G (do not expect novelty for free)
agent_test: Count emergent versus inherited attributes in the agent's blends; compare plain blend versus blend with an explicit scenario-construction step.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Emergence rises when parents conflict or are incompatible (evaluative antagonism, impossible combinations like fruit that is furniture); the person repairs the conflict by changing one concept.
agent_test: Pick seed pairs by conflict level; measure emergent-attribute rate of agent blends for low-, mid-, high-conflict pairs.

claim: Novel noun-noun phrases are not read only as a relation: relation linking, property mapping and hybrid construals all occur (about 30% property-type in Wisniewski and Gentner 1991), and similarity between the nouns favours property mapping.
schema_part: O (combine: ask for relation AND property readings)
agent_test: Prompt for three construals per pair (relation, property, hybrid) and compare idea diversity against relation-only prompting at equal tokens.

claim: Property mapping depends on salience of a modifier feature that matches a head dimension (Estes and Glucksberg: 79% vs 23% and 16%) and is higher for natural kinds than artifacts; assessed similarity per se did not predict it in Bock and Clifton once pairs were randomised, while Wisniewski 1996 found 72% vs 48% for high vs low similarity.
agent_test: Control salience separately from similarity when building seed pairs; check which predicts agent property-mapping readings.

claim: Relation-competition (CARIN) is not supported: its fit advantage comes from a free parameter (r .44 to .34), and competition distance does not predict response time (r=-.09, .08). Relation priming itself is real (143-224 ms speedups).
agent_test: Low priority; if relation priming matters, test whether a prior example with a given relation biases the agent's next blend.

claim: Ontological type of the parents predicts meaning type: artifact-artifact compounds are 93% event readings, natural-natural 15% event and 51% environmental (N=195, 148).
agent_test: Vary seed-pair ontological types and see whether the agent's relation distribution shifts like humans; use type mix to force diversity.

claim: GPT-3 matches human relation distributions for real novel compounds (r up to .93) but this collapses with nonsense words (r=.105), so success is partly memory of real words, not systematic composition.
schema_part: G (do not trust fluent blending as proof of composition)
agent_test: Test the agent on nonsense-word seed pairs with only definitions in context; a blend that survives is composition, not recall.

claim: LLMs paraphrase familiar and rare noun compounds very well (GPT-3 95.64% familiar; 83.81% vs human 73.33% novel, 105 items), though copying from web text and head/modifier swaps occur.
agent_test: Interpretation is not the bottleneck for frontier models; do not spend tokens on a separate interpretation step; test only on harder, newer compounds.

claim: Open 7B models are much weaker: 38-45% on lexicalised compounds by surprisal, strongly dependent on concreteness and relation class, and poor at transferring a relation to hypernym-swapped compounds.
agent_test: Check if the scaffold's gain is larger for small models than frontier models on compound interpretation.

claim: LLMs are worse at generating emergent properties of a combination than canceled ones (GPT-4o names property type 56.4% vs human 81%). Spread-activation prompting helps only slightly (emergent 45.1 to 45.8).
agent_test: Add an explicit 'what changes when these meet' step and measure emergent-property score on CCPT-style items at equal tokens.

claim: Across 35 LLMs, blending distant random pairs is harder than association or analogy (43.4% vs 59.0% and 53.4%). The failure is finding the shared abstraction (generic space); once found, 97.1% of blends are coherent.
schema_part: O (combine: force a shared-abstraction step first)
agent_test: Insert an explicit step that proposes the generic space before blending; compare valid-blend rate at equal tokens on distant pairs.

claim: Different LLMs invent the same properties for the same seed pair (19.9% reuse of 2+ properties, 37.3% for blends vs 2.6% for analogies; same-provider 2.3x more likely), so seed pairs give a narrower idea set than they seem. Gap search: cross-model sameness is corroborated outside blending (22 LLMs on creativity tests; 25 models on 26K queries, pairwise similarity 71-82%), so the effect is general. The blend-specific rates (19.9%, 37.3%) still come from one study.
agent_test: Measure overlap of ideas across repeated runs and across seed pairs; try more distant or randomised pairs and measure homogeneity change.

claim: Humans score below LLMs on valid-rate in the KOMBINE tasks (blend 12.8% vs 43.4%) but explore different semantic regions, so human data is a complement rather than an upper bound.
agent_test: Do not use human validity as target; measure novelty and validity separately.

claim: A fixed pipeline where code ranks and the model fills slots (expand associations, find connecting concepts, then scenes) doubled blend ideas per pair (2.03 vs 0.87) and halved mental demand in N=10 users; connecting-concept accuracy about 56-59%.
agent_test: Implement expand-connect-select as an operator and compare idea count and validity to free brainstorming at equal tokens.

claim: Language models beat a knowledge base (ConceptNet P@1000 about 5.9 vs 66.38) at proposing the shared property that a visual blend hinges on.
schema_part: O (combine: property proposal by LM, not KB)
agent_test: Compare LM-proposed versus retrieved shared properties for blend quality.

claim: Vision-language models do worse on compound nouns than on parts (CLIP 78.25% vs human 96.25%); reversing noun order hurts; LLM-written example captions add 8.25 points for CLIP and 2.35 for OpenCLIP. Text-to-image models often fail to fuse nouns (egg noodle).
agent_test: Not core to a text agent; order sensitivity matches human non-commutativity.

claim: Modern embeddings represent a compound roughly as the sum of its parts (cosine .85 simple addition, .92 ridge), and autoregressive models hold relation information at the compound's last token.
agent_test: Probe only if interpretability is added; low priority for scaffold.

claim: Quantum-probability models fit double overextension and underextension where classical probability cannot, and LLMs are reported to violate a Bell (CHSH) inequality on a combined concept; but values above the 2.83 bound (3.09, 4.0) and Hampton's sequential-projection objection leave this unsettled.
agent_test: No test needed; do not build a quantum component. Revisit only if an independent group replicates the Bell results.

claim: The guppy effect (item better member of A-and-B than of either) is real but rarer than simple overextension of one conjunct.
agent_test: Keep as a caveat when claiming that blends are surprising.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Older neural LMs did poorly on adjective-noun composition by inference (GPT-2 71.75% vs human 94.3%; non-local adjective RoBERTa 19.3% vs 89.8%); frontier models were not tested.
agent_test: Superseded by frontier models; do not rely on.

claim: Humans give more diverse associative names for image pairs than multimodal LLMs (greater semantic distance and entropy).
agent_test: Check if the agent's naming diversity falls below a human-like level; use a diversity sampling step.

claim: Wisniewski 1997 is now read in full (theory paper: comparison then construction; hybrids rise with noun similarity; 70% of 3,003 meanings of 224 novel combinations from 189 subjects construed a referent atypically). Costello and Keane 2000 (C3 constraints: diagnosticity, plausibility, informativeness) is still unopened (paywalled), so its human-match numbers and any benefit of an LLM or code filter remain untested here.
agent_test: Implement the three constraints as a filter on blends and compare retained-idea quality to unfiltered at equal tokens.

claim: A structure-first step (extract shared relational structure, choose far domains, then search) raises novelty and diversity of LLM solutions at about equal call count (2 vs 2 calls): novel-solution rate 1.6% (no-domain) and 21.6% (cross-domain) up to 50.4% for Claude Sonnet 4.5; solution diversity +90-173%. It is tested on research problems, not noun-noun blends, so the generic-space fix for blends is still untested.
schema_part: O (combine: abstract first), S1 seed choice
agent_test: On KOMBINE-style pairs, compare free blending with a two-call 'name the shared abstraction, then blend' arm at equal tokens; score valid-blend rate against the 43.4% baseline.

claim: Far-domain analogies produced downstream gains in four implemented biomedical cases (about 13-fold on a distributional metric; Spearman .729; state of the art on 2 datasets). There is no near-seed arm, only 4 cases and no replication, so 'what distance is best' is unanswered.
agent_test: Run near, medium and far seed bands on the same task set with a downstream metric and equal tokens; look for an inverted U.

claim: Homogeneity of LLM ideas is cut mainly by varied inputs plus a structured step, not by decoding or pooling. Persona+CoT gave 248 unique category combinations vs 197 for humans and 88 for default GPT-4o (N=99/83 per arm); evolved, spread-out personas raised AUT diversity +78.8% vs +8.7% for random personas. Temperature 1.5 gave marginal gain, 2.0 garbled text; min-p at T=2.0 left 81% of pairs above 0.7 similarity; creative system prompts moved AUT variability only 0.459 to 0.576 against humans at 0.738; pooling 40 GPT-4 sessions was among the least diverse (cosine 0.428).
agent_test: For blending, pick seed pairs by maximum spread in embedding space and add a CoT draft-then-revise pass; measure property reuse across 3 runs and across 2 models at equal tokens.

claim: Explicitly stating the linking event between two nouns, and the ambiguity of readings, helps LLMs: accuracy on novel-compound relations rose, e.g. GPT-4o 51.4 to 55.7 and 52.8 to 58.3, open 7B models by more than 9 points. About 55% of benchmark compounds admit more than one reading, and GPT-4o is 10-15 points lower on novel than on lexicalised compounds.
schema_part: O (combine: state relation, keep several readings)
agent_test: When blending, require the model to write the linking event and a second reading before scoring; check whether valid-blend rate rises.

claim: Gap search found no study for these: frontier-LLM membership judgments for A, B and A-and-B in both orders (overextension, non-commutativity); an LLM or code filter based on Costello and Keane constraints; PopBlends-style pipelines beyond N=10; the nonsense-word test on current models; or any large-sample (N over 200) replication of Hampton's human effects. These remain open, with the caveat that the search tools were limited.
agent_test: Run them in our own harness: 40 A/B/A-and-B items in both orders on the current model; 20 nonsense compounds with definitions given vs real compounds.
